title: Deposits, refunds and finances under the Beverage Container Return Scheme
asked: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked how much in deposits has been collected from beverage producers and retailers since the Beverage Container Return Scheme began, how much has been refunded to consumers who returned containers, and how any surplus is accounted for — whether kept by BCRS Ltd, put back into scheme operations, or returned to Government.
response: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the scheme is in a transition phase until 30 September 2026 and has handled over one million successful transactions and 5.5 million returned containers. BCRS Ltd is a not-for-profit company funded by producer fees and revenue from the sale of recyclables, and deposits paid by consumers but not redeemed may be used by BCRS Ltd to cover the costs of running the scheme. BCRS Ltd must submit an annual report to the National Environment Agency, including an account of its finances, within three months after the end of each compliance year. On return points, all 1,070 planned RVMs are deployed and operational, with a target of around 2,000 return points within the first year.
